question.question: An AI/ML engineer is deploying a distributed training workload on a Kubernetes cluster with GPU nodes. Which of the following statements about GPU resource management and pod scheduling are correct?

options.text: GPU resources are requested using the standard 'resources.limits.nvidia.com/gpu' field in the pod spec, and Kubernetes automatically schedules pods only on nodes with available GPUs.
The NVIDIA device plugin must be installed on each GPU node to advertise GPU capacity to the kubelet and enable GPU resource requests.
Setting 'resources.requests.nvidia.com/gpu: 1' and 'resources.limits.nvidia.com/gpu: 1' guarantees the pod gets exclusive access to a physical GPU device.
Using 'nvidia.com/gpu' resource requests works without any additional node labeling; the device plugin automatically handles node selection.
For multi-GPU training pods, you can request fractional GPUs (e.g., 0.5) to share a single GPU across multiple training jobs.

question.explanation: Option 2 is correct: The NVIDIA device plugin is required on each GPU node to discover GPUs and register them as allocatable resources with the kubelet. Option 3 is correct: Kubernetes GPU scheduling uses a 'limit equals request' model — you must set both request and limit to the same integer value, which guarantees exclusive access to whole physical GPUs. Option 1 is incorrect because the resource name is 'nvidia.com/gpu' (not 'resources.limits.nvidia.com/gpu' as a path). Option 4 is misleading — while the device plugin advertises capacity, you often need node selectors/affinity to target GPU node pools. Option 5 is incorrect: Kubernetes does not support fractional GPU requests; GPUs are allocated as whole devices.
concepts_tested: Resource requests and limits for GPUs
